findings.passage: “Whenever voter ID has been suggested in the past, I broke ranks, stood my ground and voted my belief that voter ID was needed to allay fears of election fraud and guarantee election integrity,” Burns said.
findings.note: Statement in his House press release after a 2023 vote for a proposal requiring voters to show ID at the polls; also says he is ready to push his own bipartisan bill.

findings.passage: “Voting is a sacred right, and we should be doing everything to protect it and restore voters’ confidence in the process, especially when so many Pennsylvanians believe ID should be required in order to vote.”
findings.note: Same release; his reason for supporting ID at the polls.

findings.passage: “It’s simple; we need to make sure that people who vote are who they say they are.
findings.note: Quote in a House release announcing HB 771 (voter ID at the polls, with a written-affirmation alternative for a voter without ID), introduced with two co-sponsors. The sentence continues in the release: 'As elected officials we need to do everything we can to alleviate fears of election fraud and guarantee election integrity'. The release describes HB 771 as letting a voter without acceptable ID affirm identity in writing.

findings.passage: We need to make sure that people who vote are who they say they are.
findings.note: Quote in a House release on his vote for HB 1300 (voter ID at the polls, signature checks for mail ballots, drop-box option).
